steps: Lift the top plate, release the two glass-frame latches, and install the certified safety barrier (157727) before operating. Review all requirements first.
Floor pad 24" × 14" min (never on carpet, vinyl, linoleum or Pergo). Rear 2" from the draft hood, sides and corner 3", ceiling 32¼". Alcove min 36"W × 24"D × 44¼"H.
Ships for natural gas. For propane, convert with kit 155592 before installing — swap to the #53 burner and #30 pilot orifices and the LP regulator tower. Authorized technician only.
Vertical B-vent only, 7–35 ft off the draft hood; ≤4 ft total horizontal; max three 90° or four 45° elbows; firestop at each floor; listed B-vent cap. Above 2000 ft, 12 ft minimum rise.
3/8" NPT supply with a manual shut-off (T-handle in MA) and union in the same room. Leak-test with soap solution — never a flame. Verify inlet and manifold pressure with a manometer on HIGH.
Install the rear, right, left and middle logs; spread embers, keeping them off the pilot carry-over ports and 1/4" clear of the burner-skirt edges. Wear gloves.
Install the blower before the gas line for clearance; ground per code. Wire the remote / thermostat to the terminal block — the red thermopile lead lands on the valve TH/TP terminal.
Purge the line on first light. Confirm the pilot engulfs the top 3/8" of the thermopile and 1/8" of the thermocouple, then adjust the air shutter for a clean flame with no soot.

panels.title: Pilot won't stay lit
items: Pilot doesn't engulf the top 3/8" of the thermopile → weak millivolt, burner drops out
Dirty or corroded thermopile / thermocouple, or a loose TH/TP connection
Pilot orifice blocked, or the wrong size after a fuel conversion
Embers or debris covering the pilot carry-over ports

panels.title: Spill switch tripping / draft
items: Blocked or disassembled vent, or an obstructed termination cap
Down-draft or flow reversal — common on outside or basement chimneys
House depressurization competing with the atmospheric B-vent
Vent under 7 ft / over 35 ft, or more than 4 ft of horizontal run

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
Before lighting, smell all around the stove for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop — see Safety & gas smell.
Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob will not push in or turn by hand, do not try to repair it. Call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

This stove has a standing pilot you light by hand with the spark ignitor.

  1. Open the lower control door and set the rear ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF.
  2. Confirm the gas supply shut-off valve is open.
  3. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Wait 5 minutes. Still smell gas? Stop.
  4. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counter-clockwise to PILOT.
  5. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Press the red spark ignitor button repeatedly until the pilot lights, then keep holding about one minute.
  6. Release the knob — it should spring back and the pilot stays lit. If it goes out, repeat from step 3.
  7. Turn the knob counter-clockwise to ON.
  8. Set the rear rocker switch to ON (or set your thermostat).
First light after the gas was off takes a moment while air purges from the line. If the pilot won't stay lit after several tries, turn the knob to OFF and call a service technician.

flame.title: Adjusting the flame & heat
flame.html:
The HI/LOW knob in the center of the valve face sets flame height and heat output — up to about a 50% swing between low and high. Turn it to dial in your level.

Use only the HI/LOW knob. Don't try to change the flame by setting the gas valve in any position other than full ON.

If the flame looks wrong

Long yellow flames and soot (black deposits on the logs or glass) mean the air shutter needs adjusting — that's a job for a qualified technician, not a homeowner setting.

remote.title: Remote & thermostat
remote.html:
The stove works with an optional low-voltage (750 mV) wall thermostat or remote receiver.

  1. Light the pilot first (see Light the stove) — the pilot is what powers the control.
  2. Set the rear rocker switch to T-STAT.
  3. Operate from the thermostat or remote per its own instructions.
Wiring is an installer job. The thermostat runs on a two-wire millivolt circuit, and the burner only responds in the T-STAT position with the pilot lit.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
Pause the flame

Set the rear rocker switch to OFF. The pilot stays lit for normal standby.

Turn off the pilot too

Open the lower control door, push the gas control knob in slightly, and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.

Shut it down fully

Close the supply-line gas cock.

pilot.title: Checking the pilot flame
pilot.html:
You can see the pilot through the small view port at the rear, under the right log.

A healthy pilot is steady — not lifting or floating — blue around the hood with a little yellow at the edges, and reaches about 1 inch out of all three ports.

Weak or won't stay lit? That's a service call — have a technician check the pilot, thermopile and thermocouple.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Never clean the glass while it's hot, never use abrasive cleaners, and never run the stove with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  1. Let the glass cool completely.
  2. Wipe with a clean, damp soft cloth.
  3. Dry with a soft towel, taking care not to scratch the surface.

A little "fog" on the glass each time you light it is normal and clears as the glass warms.

Replacement glass is the Jøtul Ceramic Glass Replacement Kit 155599 only — no substitutes.

blower.title: Running the blower
blower.html:
The optional variable-speed blower pushes warm air off the firebox and into the room.

AUTOturns on once the stove heats, off when it cools
MANUALruns regardless of temperature
OFFblower off

Use the rheostat knob to set the fan speed.

sounds.title: Odors, fog & the first few fires
sounds.html:
A faint odor or some smoke at first

During the first few fires it's normal to smell manufacturing residue burning off and materials curing. Open a window and let fresh air move through; it passes.

Fog on the glass

Condensation each time you light the stove is normal and clears as the glass warms up.

A strong gas smell is different. If you smell gas, don't light anything and don't touch switches or phones inside. Leave and immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone. See Safety & gas smell.

safety.title: Safety & what to do if you smell gas
safety.html:
• Surfaces and the glass get very hot — keep children and at-risk individuals away.
  • The certified safety barrier (157727) reduces burn risk at the glass and must be installed; if it's ever damaged, replace it with the same part before using the stove.
  • Never store or use gasoline or flammable liquids near the stove.
  • Gas or propane only — never burn wood, paper or any solid fuel in it.
  • Do not use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that may have been under water.
If you smell gas: Extinguish any open flame. Open windows. Do NOT try to light anything. Do NOT touch electrical switches or use any phone in the building. Leave and immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone. Follow the gas supplier's instructions. If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.
Massachusetts: a carbon-monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the appliance.

service.title: Annual service & warranty
service.html:
Have the stove and its vent inspected and cleaned at least once a year by a qualified technician. Always shut off the gas (and unplug the blower) before any service.

Cast iron, firebox5 years
Burner, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish2 years
Gas & electrical (valve, controls, blower)1 year
This is a summary. The full warranty terms and exclusions are in the official PDF.

specInput.title: Input rates
specInput.html:
NG max / min26,000 / 15,000 BTU/hr
LP max / min26,000 / 15,500 BTU/hr
Maker's website: Min LPO input 13500. Install to the manual.

EnerGuide rating 58.68% (CSA P.4.1-15). Orifice sizing changes on fuel conversion — see the conversion kit (155592 to LP, 155593 back to NG).

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0 – 7.0 in. WC
Propane12.0 – 14.9 in. WC

Measure at the E (inlet) test point on the front of the valve with the control knob on HIGH. An external regulator is required for propane.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.2 – 3.8 in. WC
Propane2.9 – 11.0 in. WC

Measure at the A (manifold) test point, knob on HIGH. The pilot should be blue at the hood with yellow at the edges, project ~1", and engulf the top 3/8" of the thermopile and the top 1/8" of the thermocouple.

specVent.title: Venting — 4" Type B
specVent.html:
Natural-vent / B-vent only. Exactly 4" Type B pipe, vertical, vented directly outside. Never connect to a chimney serving any other appliance. Single-wall connector pipe is prohibited.
Pipe4" Type B (or listed flex gas liner)
Height off draft hood7 ft min · 35 ft max
Total horizontal4 ft max
Elbows≤ three 90° or four 45°

Slope horizontal runs 1/4" per foot up toward the cap; firestop at each floor; a listed B-vent termination cap is required. Above 2000 ft, the minimum vertical rise is 12 ft.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Measured from the stove body, standard legs. With short legs, subtract 2¼" from floor-referenced figures.

Rear (from draft hood)2"
Sides3"
Corner3"
Ceiling (from stove top)32¼"

Vent-pipe clearances: 1" on all sides of vertical runs; 2" top, sides and bottom on horizontal runs. Minimum alcove 36"W × 24"D × 44¼"H.

specHearth.title: Hearth / floor protection
specHearth.html:
Minimum pad24" W × 14" D
Coveragefull width & depth of the stove

The stove cannot sit directly on carpet, vinyl, linoleum or Pergo. On any combustible other than wood, install a metal or wood pad, or a listed hearth pad. Carpet, vinyl or linoleum may remain underneath the floor protection.

notes: Oct 12 report-everything pass: the content converted from the v2 guide had no review block, so there were no in-manual conflicts on file to classify. Website rows not compared because the manual does not cover them: weight, heating capacity, item numbers per finish. Height / width / depth / short-leg height: the manual's p. 4 drawing prints 25" (635 mm) and 16 1/2" (419 mm) and says short legs reduce height by 2 1/4" (57 mm), but its text does not say what the two dimensions measure, so they were not compared with the website's figures. The other input rates, the 50% turn-down (p. 17), the included barrier and the top/rear flue exit (157724 kit, p. 4) agree with the website.
